questions.q: Describe and explain how the body responds when a person walks into a very cold place. Portal response box.
questions.a: Temperature receptors detect the fall (1); brain coordinates (1); vasoconstriction (1) reduces blood flow near the surface, less heat lost (1); shivering (1) muscles respire releasing heat (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes: 'Temperature receptors detect that the body is cooling.'

questions.q: Why is sweating less effective in humid air?
questions.a: Air is already full of water vapour (1), so sweat evaporates slowly and less heat is lost (1)

questions.q: Why can a high fever be dangerous?
questions.a: Enzymes may denature above about 40 °C, so metabolism is disrupted.

questions.q: Explain how sweating cools the body.
questions.a: Sweat evaporates from the skin (1), transferring energy from the skin to the surroundings (1)
questions.model: Sweat is water on the skin. It evaporates. Evaporation needs energy, taken from the skin. So the skin cools.

questions.a: Narrowing of blood vessels near the skin surface

questions.q: Name two conditions kept constant by homeostasis.
questions.a: Body temperature and water content (also blood glucose)
